Pull request description:

  Part of #36692. Follow-up to #36750

  Replaces field-by-field construction of inputs and outputs with `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` ctor calls in `txpackage_tests`, `bench/duplicate_inputs` and `script_p2sh_tests`.

  `CMutableTransaction` is kept as the builder while a `CTransaction` constructor is discussed in #36696. Witnesses are still assigned after `vin`, since `CTxIn` has no witness argument yet.

  Test-only; the constructed transactions are unchanged.

  - `script_p2sh_tests`: two outputs created by `vout.resize(1)` never had a value, so their null `nValue` (`-1`) is now explicit.
  - Intentional mutations are left as they are: the `scriptSig` swap in `sign`, the dummy signing in `ValidateInputsStandardness`, and the witness-only copies in `txpackage_tests` (`mtx_child2`, `mtx_parent2_v2`).

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36252: ci, iwyu: skip subtrees in compilation database

01e3eca2d8ee755eed4488a44093759f0eddcb34 ci, iwyu: skip subtrees in compilation database (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The IWYU CI job analyzes `src/ipc/libmultiprocess/` even though its results are thrown away. Every run prints IWYU suggestions for 14 libmultiprocess files in the non-enforced pass, applies them, and then reverts them with the `git restore` from #36112. The suggestions also disagree with what libmultiprocess's own IWYU CI reports (it runs with `-Xiwyu --error` and passes), because the two jobs use different IWYU versions and mapping files. libmultiprocess is the only subtree in this situation; leveldb, crc32c, minisketch and secp256k1 are already excluded from `compile_commands.json` with `EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS OFF`. #35361 reported this output and said IWYU shouldn't be running on subtrees.

  **Solution:** Filter `SHARED_EXCLUDED_SUBTREES` (from `test/lint/lint_ignore_dirs.py`) out of `compile_commands.json` at the start of the IWYU section of `ci/test/03_test_script.sh`, so subtree sources are neither analyzed nor edited. This is done in the CI script rather than in cmake so that only IWYU is affected: clang-tidy keeps running on libmultiprocess, and no list of subtree targets has to be maintained in `cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake` (that approach broke `-DBUILD_TESTS=OFF` in #35418 and was reverted in #35523). The change is three lines in `ci/test/03_test_script.sh`; the rest of the diff is comments.

  **Testing note:** You can confirm this works by checking the IWYU CI logs and confirming that output like `/home/runner/work/_temp/src/ipc/libmultiprocess/src/mp/gen.cpp should add these lines:` no longer appears.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36772: test: Remove `BOOST_FAIL` and add info in descriptor_tests

f5a887c199613be9ddc8a13fbb7934af614fa579 test: Remove `BOOST_FAIL` and add info in descriptor_tests (rustaceanrob)

Pull request description:

  The `BOOST_FAIL` here is used to exit the test based on a condition, but we can use `REQUIRE` directly. The context string is only printed on failure to my knowledge and this is not called on a child thread so there is no behavior change.

  The `descriptor_tests` uses `BOOST_TEST_INFO` to add the descriptor if the next condition fails, but there are some other places that also print the public or private descriptor. Seems useful throughout this whole funciton body to attach the private and public descriptor as context.

  Found in #35713 as low usage macros

  ref:
  - https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testout_reference/test_output_macro_info.html
  - https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testout_reference/test_output_macro_context_sticky.html
  - https://www.boost.org/doc/libs/latest/libs/test/doc/html/boost_test/utf_reference/testing_tool_ref/assertion_boost_fail.html

test: construct script_p2sh_tests inputs/outputs declaratively

Replace field-by-field construction of inputs and outputs with
COutPoint, CTxIn and CTxOut constructor calls.

Outputs previously created by vout.resize() without a value now spell
out the null nValue (-1) explicitly. Loop indices become uint32_t to
match COutPoint::n, since brace-initialization rejects the narrowing.

The scriptSig mutations after signing are intentional and kept.

The constructed transactions are unchanged.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36613: test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks

64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897 test: add getblockfilter test coverage for header-only blocks (Aaron Leeb)

Pull request description:

  Add functional coverage for the `getblockfilter` error raised when a node has a known block header, but the block has never been connected.

  This gap in test coverage was identified by a coverage report generated while exploring BIP 157/158. The branch in `src/rpc/blockchain.cpp` was never executed in the measured tests:
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/64cf455b481d36182957bdcfcae7c411a7879897/src/rpc/blockchain.cpp#L3054-L3056

  The existing `getblockfilter` functional test checks unknown block hashes and filter retrieval for active and stale blocks, but doesn’t check a known header whose block has never been connected.

  This change submits only the block header of a newly mined block to a node using `submitheader` and verifies that in this expected state, `getblockfilter` returns error `-5` with `"Filter not found. Block was not connected to active chain."` This adds coverage for the RPC’s distinction between an unknown block and a known block for which no filter has been constructed.

  `rpc_getblockfilter.py` passes, and changing the error message makes the new assertion fail as expected.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36591: test: deduplicate PSBT unknown-field coverage in `rpc_psbt.py`

ef4310097bd651497a98a9d1bb59560a7055ae01 test: combine redundant PSBT unknown field merge cases into `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields` (nebula-21)
40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 test: extract unknown fields passthrough to its own method (nebula-21)

Pull request description:

  I've tested some mutations related to test coverage for PSBT unknown field merging and discovered an inconsistency.
  <details>

  If line 71 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(psbt.unknown.begin(), psbt.unknown.end());`"  (inside `bool PartiallySignedTransaction::Merge(const PartiallySignedTransaction& psbt)` function) is removed then, the expected test fails: *"Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map."*

  If line 434 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(input.unknown.begin(), input.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTInput::Merge(const PSBTInput& input)` function), is removed, a different unexpected test fails: "*Test that unknown values are just passed through*".

  If line 537 of `psbt.cpp` "`unknown.insert(output.unknown.begin(), output.unknown.end());`" (inside `bool PSBTOutput::Merge(const PSBTOutput& output)` function), is removed, the expected test fails: "*Test that combining PSBTs preserves unknown fields with the same and with distinct values per map.*".
  </details>

  This PR solves this inconsistency.
  The old code did 3 different things:
  1. Test the pass-through of unknown values for `walletprocesspsbt`.
  2. Combine two v0 PSBTs with different unknown input keys and check that both keys survive.
  3. Combine implicit v0 PSBT with explicit v0 and check that both keys survive.

  Case 2 is already fully covered by the existing `test_combinepsbt_preseves_unknown_fields` so keeping it is redundant and misleading.

  Commit 40eba5eb20ba0041a6328ba3482fcc26ddbe0185 moves the old code into a new method called `test_unknown_fields_passthrough` and commit ef4310097bd651497a98a9d1bb59560a7055ae01 removes the redundant code of Case 2 and moves Case 3 inside `test_combinepsbt_preserves_unknown_fields`.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36475: bench: add BIP-352 pubkey extraction benchmarks (standard + P2PKH worst-case)

56c0f168d1a81b19e4cd71ef81e7ce2d9c1624e3 bench: add worst-case P2PKH benchmark for BIP-352 pubkey extraction (Sebastian Falbesoner)
d71bc7127f0ce06da96476456160799e817f0a14 bench: add benchmarks for BIP-352 pubkey extraction (standard inputs) (Sebastian Falbesoner)

Pull request description:

  As there are ongoing changes to the Silent Payments public key extraction function `GetPubKeyFromInput` (see recently merged #36338), it seems reasonable to add benchmarks for it. The first commit covers the standard shape of each eligible input type (P2PKH, P2SH-P2WPKH, P2WPKH and P2TR script-path spend; see [BIP-352](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/blob/master/bip-0352.mediawiki#user-content-Inputs_For_Shared_Secret_Derivation)). The second adds a worst-case P2PKH input with a maximally malleated scriptSig, where every push has to be hashed during the scan.

  Results on my arm64 machine (as per `$ ./build/bin/bench_bitcoin -filter='BIP352_.*'`):

  |            ns/input |             input/s |    err% |     total | benchmark
  |--------------------:|--------------------:|--------:|----------:|:----------
  |            3,034.12 |          329,584.35 |    0.2% |      0.01 | `BIP352_GetPubKey_P2PKH`
  |           69,868.20 |           14,312.66 |    0.1% |      0.01 | `BIP352_GetPubKey_P2PKH_WorstCase`
  |            2,841.35 |          351,945.44 |    0.1% |      0.01 | `BIP352_GetPubKey_P2SH_P2WPKH`
  |            2,768.00 |          361,272.01 |    0.1% |      0.01 | `BIP352_GetPubKey_P2TR`
  |            2,757.57 |          362,637.66 |    0.0% |      0.01 | `BIP352_GetPubKey_P2WPKH`

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36694: test: construct `mempool_tests` inputs/outputs declaratively

b7abd88f0f2838b26a09a30e4aa23f18806b962f test: construct mempool_tests inputs/outputs declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)

Pull request description:

  Part of #36692. This replaces the field-by-field construction of transaction inputs and outputs in `mempool_tests` with `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` constructor calls.

  It keeps `CMutableTransaction` as the builder, since a `CTransaction` constructor taking inputs and outputs directly is still under discussion (#36696). If one is added, the `vin`/`vout` lists here can be passed to it directly. Either way, the declarative form makes the constructed transactions easier to read.

  This change is test-only and does not change the constructed transactions.

  The `mempool_eviction` bench and `rbf_tests` changes from the earlier version of this PR have been dropped, as they conflict with #36521. They can follow once that is resolved.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36765: fuzz: push messages to one of m_nodes in connman target

ad51e87ecfd8f4b27e703b5c6116e6d75dcb9787 fuzz: push a message to an actually connected node in connman target (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  The connman fuzz target never exercised `m_nodes` peers with queued messages, as their message queue is always empty. The most they ever had to send was handshake bytes in the case of v2 peers, so the socket handler only ever waited for SendEvent, and sent data, during a v2 handshake.

  Fix this by pushing messages to one of the `m_nodes` peers instead of `random_node`, which is never added to connman.

a7d3a4297321274ced64294e0bbd3252167e8879 test: use monotonic clock in interface_http (ViniciusCestarii)
eccca10e6460507e553e61a1cdaf664fa7738375 test: use monotonic clock for durations in test framework (ViniciusCestarii)

Pull request description:

  Replace `time.time()` used to measure durations by `time.monotonic()` in test framework and http_interface.

  This helps preventing future clock jump flakiness (same class of bug as #36529) on tests and fix:

  ```
  faketime --exclude-monotonic -f "+0 x0.5" build/test/functional/feature_torcontrol.py

  ```
